title: Bounded complementary monomials span the generated subfield
statement:
Let p be prime, k a field of characteristic p [def-weil-field], I any index type, t : I → k, and J a finite subset of I. Let F be the intermediate field F_p(k^p) generated by the pth powers, and let kJ be the subfield generated by all pth powers and t_i for i outside J. Every element of kJ lies in the F-span in k of the bounded finitely supported monomials whose exponents vanish on J. No p-basis assumption is made. Complete formal statement:
theorem pBasisComplementMonomial_mem_span
    (p : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime] (k : Type u) [Field k] [CharP k p]
    (I : Type w) (t : I → k) (J : Finset I) (kJ : Subfield k)
    (hkJ : kJ = Subfield.closure
      (Set.range (fun x : k ↦ x ^ p) ∪ {x : k | ∃ i : I, i ∉ J ∧ t i = x}))
    (a : kJ) :
    (a : k) ∈ Submodule.span
      (IntermediateField.adjoin (ZMod p) (Set.range (fun x : k ↦ x ^ p)))
      (Set.range (fun D : {D : I →₀ ℕ //
        (∀ i, D i < p) ∧ ∀ i ∈ J, D i = 0} ↦
        (D : I →₀ ℕ).prod (fun i e ↦ t i ^ e)))

source.place: Tag 07P5, proof first paragraph: the coefficient subfield k_J; expanded bounded-monomial argument

proof.text: Put F = F_p(k^p), and let W be the F-span of the bounded complementary monomials. The zero exponent function gives 1 in W. Every pth power is in F by the generating property of IntermediateField.adjoin. For a complementary finitely supported exponent D, define R_i = D_i mod p and q = product_i t_i^(D_i div p). Then R is bounded and complementary and t^D = q^p t^R, since D_i = p(D_i div p) + R_i. This proves every unbounded complementary monomial lies in W.

Multiplying two bounded complementary monomials adds their exponent functions, so their product lies in W by the preceding exponent reduction. Induction on the two span presentations proves W is closed under multiplication: the generating case uses that identity, and the zero, addition and scalar cases use distributivity. Induction on n then gives a^n in W whenever a is in W.

If a in W is zero, its inverse is zero. Otherwise a^p is nonzero and belongs to F, and a inverse = (a^p) inverse times a^(p-1). Scalar closure and the power closure just proved put this inverse in W. Thus W, with its existing additive closure, 1, multiplication and inversion, is a subfield.

Each pth power is an F-scalar times 1, hence is in W. For i outside J, the single exponent function at i has complementary support; its monomial is t_i and belongs to W by the unbounded-monomial result. Therefore the defining subfield closure k_J is contained in W. Apply this inclusion to the given element a.
